findings.summary: crates/app/src/main.rs:55-81: the web build's fetch (status check, JSON parse, 'the answer wasn't a board' wording) is still in the app, not in board-core. So the web build doesn't name failure causes the way ReadError does: a 401/redirect from Access shows as a raw status or fetch error. The ticket scopes the shared read to native, so this isn't blocking. Worth noting for AC-8's 'reading through the shared crate': the web build shares Reads, Settings and words, but not the read itself.

crates/core/src/words.rs has no tests of its own. It is covered only through the app's render tests, and changing the 'checks unknown' wording passed all tests (an_unknown_check_state_reads_as_unknown checks deserialization, not the drawn text). Android (TRU-31) will use words without the egui render tests, so direct tests in crates/core/tests would keep the clients' wording pinned.

crates/server/src/metrics.rs:client: any User-Agent starting 'Mozilla/' counts as web, so browser-like bots or scripts land in web, not other. The label can't grow beyond four values (checked live), so this is about accuracy, not cardinality.
